Description

Director of Engineering Job Description

Exempt

Summary (Position Description)

The Director of Engineering at BITZER US is a critical executive leadership role responsible for directing, strategic planning, and overseeing all engineering activities across the organization. This position provides technical and operational leadership to a robust engineering department—including problem resolution and system development—to ensure design integrity, innovation, production efficiency, and compliance with BITZER’s world-class quality benchmarks.

Executing these duties to align with broader company objectives, the Director partners closely with executive management to establish strategic technical direction and implement rigorous controls. By driving accountability through a structured team of Engineering Managers and Supervisors, the Director champions operational excellence from initial concepts all the way through to final production.

Key Information

Reports To:
Vice President of Operations

Direct Reports:
Engineering Managers, Engineering Supervisors

Location:
In Office at 4080 Enterprise Way, Flowery Branch, GA 30542

There will be some traveling, including to Europe 2-3 times a year

Travel Requirements:
Domestic and international travel required, including traveling to European corporate headquarters 2–3 times per year.

Who We Are

Bitzer Us Inc. is a leading manufacturer of key components used in commercial and industrial refrigeration and air conditioning systems. These key components include compressors, pressure vessels such as condensers and evaporators, compressor packages, and condensing units. Other products include waste heat-to-power equipment that converts excess heat to low-cost electricity.

You partner with others to get work done while gaining insight into customers' needs and deliver solutions that exceed customer expectations. You create Raving Fans. You set objectives aligning with organization and prioritize accordingly.

Conveniently located in Flowery Branch, Georgia 5 minutes off I-985 The Company is wholly owned by Bitzer SE (located in Germany), the Company is a private company and serves as Bitzer SE’s flagship North American subsidiary. On a global basis, Bitzer SE has 3,400 employees in 60 locations with global sales approaching 700M €.

Essential Duties & Responsibilities

Strategic & Operational Leadership

Provide overarching leadership and strategic vision to the entire engineering department, aligning engineering goals with BITZER US operational and corporate objectives.
Foster a collaborative, high-performance culture focused on continuous improvement, technical excellence, and professional development.
Manage and optimize the engineering department budget, resource allocation, and project pipelines to meet strict production deadlines.

Technical & Design Oversight

Hold overall responsibility for Engineering activities across the business, including: Product Sustaining Engineering, Development Engineering, Advanced Technology, and Engineering Services
Oversee the creation, modification, and strict configuration control of highly technical, part-specific engineering drawings, specifications, and Bills of Materials (BOMs).
Ensure absolute design integrity, compliance with global BITZER standards, and adherence to relevant industry regulations (e.g., ASME, UL, ISO).
Create and implement best practice engineering vision, strategy, policies, processes, and procedures to aid and improve business performance
Ensure that engineering strategies and processes are in place to meet business objectives and operational needs in terms of price, quality, and delivery targets and which enables the company to function and compete effectively in the market
Drive the optimization of engineering software, PLM (Product Lifecycle Management), and CAD systems to maximize department efficiency and accuracy.
Collaborate closely with Quality Assurance and Manufacturing Engineering to resolve complex design-related production issues and execute precise Engineering Change Notices (ECNs).

Cross-Functional Collaboration

Partner tightly with the VP of Operations to streamline the transition of products from design/prototype stages into full-scale manufacturing.
Function as a key technical liaison with global engineering teams at corporate headquarters, ensuring alignment on product platforms and technology sharing.
Work alongside Procurement and Supply Chain to evaluate vendor capabilities and technical compliance for component manufacturing.

Competencies (Knowledge, Skills & Abilities)

Expertise in industrial engineering drawing standards, GD&T (Geometric Dimensioning and Tolerancing), and PLM systems.
Proven record of managing complex engineering pipelines for products with high part counts and specialized component configurations.
Exceptional leadership and communication skills, with the ability to translate complex technical concepts into clear operational milestones for leadership.
Experience navigating cross-functional systems (such as SAP or similar advanced ERP architecture) is highly beneficial.
Strong understanding of Business Financial Management and departmental budgeting.
Strategic thinker with a proven ability to solve complex problems through data analysis.
Commitment to corporate ethics and professional conduct.

Requirements

Education: Bachelor of Science in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a closely related technical field is required. A Master’s degree or MBA is highly desirable.
Experience: 10+ years of progressive engineering experience in a highly technical, precision manufacturing environment (experience with compressors, pressure vessels, or HVAC-R systems is a significant plus).
Leadership: 5+ years of formal leadership experience managing multi-tiered engineering teams (including managing other engineering managers/supervisors).
Ability to effectively meet and communicate with employees, the public, and vendors using courtesy, discretion, and sound judgment.
Solid professional PC skills, including advanced proficiency with the Microsoft Office Suite.
Strong written communication skills and effective, corporate-level organizational abilities.
Proven ability to work collectively and collaboratively with leadership across all arms of the organization.

Work Environment

This job is primarily performed in a professional office environment utilizing standard computer equipment. Periodically, the role requires time spent on the production and assembly floor, which requires adherence to all safety protocols and the consistent use of proper Personal Protective Equipment (PPE).

Physical Demands

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to talk and hear. The employee is frequently required to stand, walk, bend, stoop, reach with hands and arms, and use hands to finger, handle, or feel. The employee may occasionally be required to lift or move technical components weighing up to 50 pounds during floor evaluations.

CarMax is looking for a Director, AI/ML Engineering to lead and scale our artificial intelligence, and ML capabilities. The AI/ML Engineering team is the engineering arm powering next-generation AI solutions — including agentic AI systems, generative AI applications, and intelligent automation workflows — as well as core machine learning models such as vehicle pricing, personalized recommender on carmax.com, ad-bidding, and computer vision. We are looking for highly motivated individuals comfortable in a dynamic environment, experience leading 50+ member teams (comprised of FTEs & contractors), and with a solid track record in AI engineering, generative AI, agentic systems, and Machine Learning technology and platform.

The role requires ability to step into multiple roles ranging from technical product manager, team mentor, and technical architect. This position is ideal for individuals with high accountability, developing future leaders, strong analytical skills, financial skills, great communication style, a partnership mentality, and comfort turning facts into recommendations. The individual must be able to influence cross-functional business partners and effectively provide the Technology point-of-view on complex business issues to senior management, team members, and partners.

As a Director for AI/ML Engineering, you will:
Establish a technology vision and strategy for AI engineering — spanning agentic AI, generative AI, AI workflow automation, machine learning engineering, platform, and services, focusing on business outcomes tracked via key metrics, including overall financial management
Define and execute a roadmap for Agentic AI systems — autonomous, multi-step AI agents that take action on behalf of customers and associates — integrating with existing ML and data science platforms

Foster a product engineering culture within the team and establish best practices around discovery, prototyping, continuous and rapid testing, and learning, with a relentless focus on delivering customer value
Establish responsible AI governance practices, including safety, bias mitigation, explainability, and compliance guardrails for generative and agentic AI systems
Collaborate with other Product Managers and Architects on the design and integration with other products and/or technology platforms
Collaborate with other key stakeholders (e.g., legal, security, etc.) to ensure product features meet all security and privacy requirements — with particular attention to data governance and safety requirements for generative AI and agentic systems
Partner with Reliability Engineering team to ensure proper controls have been implemented for proactive monitoring of critical product features, availability, and stability

Proven technology leader with experience building and managing highly engaged teams
Passionate about AI engineering — including agentic AI, generative AI, and AI automation — as well as Data Science and Machine Learning engineering
Persuasive communicator – able to explain complex or intangible concepts to stakeholders at all levels

Experience managing, training and mentoring others in Engineering methodologies and best practices
Able to easily motivate and inspire team members, peers, stakeholders and executives
Innovative; thinks beyond boundaries

Continuous improvement mentality; never satisfied
Comfortable speaking to large audiences and executives
Flexible and open-minded; proactively seeks input from others
Entrepreneurial drive and spirit; enjoys working in a fast-paced environment
Handles constructive criticism with ease; adapts easily and efficiently to change

10+ years' experience in AI engineering, generative AI, or Data Science/Machine Learning or related engineering field. Experience with large language models (LLMs), agentic AI frameworks, and AI automation platforms is highly preferred. ML Ops experience is a plus.
5+ years' experience managing direct reports

Role Summary

Director, Platform Engineering

At Mastercard, the pace of change across technology, AI, and the nature of work requires that we constantly push the boundaries for the technologies in building and operating infrastructure and applications globally. The Director, Platform Engineering is a critical technology and engineering leadership role within Operations Automation Program accountable for advancing our infrastructure and platform automation strategy through innovation and effective problem-solving. This role focuses on analyzing, coding, and delivering software and platform solutions. Operations Automation program supports Mastercard’s global infrastructure footprint by building and maintain automation platforms, automating infrastructure, services, and application delivery with efficient tools and processes.

The Director, Platform Engineering is a hands-on technical expert responsible for designing, building, and maintaining automation frameworks, platform services, and Infrastructure as Code (IaC) capabilities that power large scale, hybrid infrastructure environments. Focuses on engineering reusable automation patterns, enabling self-service infrastructure delivery, and improving reliability, consistency, and velocity across cloud and on prem platforms. The ideal candidate brings hands on experience with infrastructure automation tools like Terraform, Ansible or Chef, strong DevOps engineering skills, and a passion for building scalable automation solutions.

Key Responsibilities

Design, build, and maintain Infrastructure as Code solutions using platforms like Terraform, Ansible, Chef to automate provisioning across cloud and on prem environments.
Develop reusable modules, playbooks, and automation libraries that standardize infrastructure deployment patterns.
Engineer and enhance platform services, including CI/CD pipelines, secrets management, artifact repositories, and configuration management systems.
Implement automated testing, validation, and security scanning for IaC and platform components.
Integrate automation with cloud platforms, virtualization systems, network/security appliances, and enterprise tooling.
Implement drift detection, compliance checks, and automated remediation workflows.
Collaborate with cloud, network, security, and SRE teams to define automation standards and best practices.
Troubleshoot complex infrastructure, automation, and CI/CD issues across hybrid environments.
Contribute to documentation, architectural diagrams, and engineering design reviews.

5–8+ years of experience in DevOps, platform engineering, cloud engineering, or infrastructure automation roles.
Strong hands-on experience with Terraform, Ansible or Chef
Solid understanding of cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, or GCP) and on prem infrastructure (VMware, Linux, networking fundamentals).
Experience building and maintaining CI/CD pipelines using GitHub Actions, GitLab, Jenkins, or Azure DevOps.
Strong scripting or programming skills (Python, Go, or similar).

Experience with configuration management, secrets management, and artifact repositories.

Familiarity with GitOps workflows and declarative infrastructure patterns.
Strong troubleshooting skills across infrastructure, automation, and platform layers.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience developing or extending Terraform modules or custom providers.
Experience with Ansible Collections, dynamic inventories, or Ansible Tower/Ansible Automation Platform.
Experience with policy as code tools (OPA and Sentinel).
Experience with monitoring, observability, and logging platforms.
Exposure to SRE practices and reliability engineering.

Core Technical Skills (Competency Areas)

Infrastructure as Code

Terraform (modules, workspaces, state management)
Ansible (playbooks, roles, collections, automation controller)
VMware, Linux, virtualization, hybrid networking
DevOps & CI/CD
Pipeline design and automation
Python, Go, or PowerShell
Self-service automation
Configuration management
Observability and operational tooling

Works within a platform engineering or DevOps organization to build automation capabilities used across the enterprise.
Collaborates closely with:
Cloud engineering
Network and security teams
SRE and operations
Application development teams
Architecture and governance groups
Acts as a subject matter expert for IaC, automation patterns, and DevOps tooling.
Contributes to engineering standards, reusable patterns, and platform roadmaps.

Complete all periodic mandatory security trainings in accordance with Mastercard’s guidelines.

added.description:
NVIDIA DGX Cloud is the AI supercomputing-as-a-service substrate designed to power the next generation of AI and industrial-scale breakthroughs. As an Engineering Manager within our Infrastructure Security Engineering organization, you will enable the engineers who secure a GPU fleet numbering in the hundreds of thousands. Your team does not write reports about risk. It engineers whole classes of risk out of existence, and delivers the result as paved roads the rest of DGX Cloud will happily take.

What You Will Be Doing

Grow the Team: Manage, coach, and develop a distributed team of senior security and infrastructure engineers. You own hiring, growth, and performance, and you build a bench deep enough that our capability never rests on one person. Heroics signal a system that needs fixing, so you protect sustainable pace.
Set Technical Direction: Partner with your engineers on the roadmap for our security control plane, our foundational security services, and the path toward autonomous security operations. Leadership owns the mission and the strategy; the team owns the execution.
Deliver Outcomes, Not Tickets: Run a lightweight planning rhythm where the team commits to a result and the reason it matters, then reflects openly on what to change next. We are measured by the risks we eliminate, not the tickets we close.
Assemble Teams Around the Work: Staff each effort with the smallest group who can deliver it, and a clear owner accountable for landing it. Teams form around the work and dissolve when it's done. Make that motion fast, fair, and a real growth opportunity.
Raise the Engineering Bar: Hold a high standard for what "done" means: tested code, observability, operational readiness, and documentation someone who didn't build the system can operate from. AI-assisted work ships with real human ownership behind it.
Communicate Risk Upward: Translate a complex, fast-moving risk picture into something executives can act on. Declare the unknowns honestly, turn risk assessment into measurable themes, and make trade-offs legible to the people funding them.
Multi-Functional Collaboration: Build the partnerships that make the work land. We operate horizontally across vertically organized teams, with influence rather than authority. Your credibility with DGX Cloud platform, SRE, networking, and broader NVIDIA security partners is a delivery mechanism, not a nicety.

What We Need To See

We are looking for high-caliber engineering leaders with deep spikes of expertise in a few of these areas and the intellectual curiosity to dive into the rest. If your experience aligns with the core of this role—building and growing teams that engineer risk out of existence—and you can show us how, we want to hear from you!

Engineering Management: Experience (7+ years) managing engineers, within a broader career (14+ years) across software engineering, SRE, infrastructure, or security. You have grown people, not only shipped projects.
Technical Credibility: Enough hands-on depth in infrastructure, distributed systems, or security engineering to earn the trust of senior engineers. You can review a design honestly and recognize when an estimate doesn't add up. You don't need to be the best engineer in the room; you need to build the room.
Hiring and Developing Talent: A history of attracting, hiring, and growing excellent engineers, including people far more expert than you in their domain. You build interview and calibration practices that make hiring repeatable and fair.
Delivery Under Ambiguity: You can take a high-stakes, loosely defined mandate and turn it into sequenced, measurable delivery. You are comfortable proving a model on a few systems first, then using that success to expand.
Cloud-Native and Security Fluency: Working understanding of cloud-native architecture, container orchestration (Kubernetes), identity and access, policy enforcement, and vulnerability management—enough to build it and ask the questions that matter.
Influence Without Authority: Experience delivering through partner teams you do not own, in environments where relationships, not org charts, determine whether the work ships.
Foundation: Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related technical field (or equivalent experience).

Ways To Stand Out From The Crowd

HPC/AI Infrastructure: Experience running teams that secure or operate high-performance computing environments, large GPU fleets, or multi-tenant platforms at cloud scale.
Security as an Internal Product: You have delivered security or infrastructure capabilities with real adoption metrics, where teams took the paved road because it was the easiest path.
Building a Function from Scratch: Experience standing up a team, a practice, or an engineering culture where none existed—charter, agreements, rituals, and all.
Scaling Without Dilution: A history of growing a team quickly while the bar went up rather than down. How have you scaled a team and raised the standard at the same time?

About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About The Role

Anthropic's Business Technology Engineering team builds the systems the company runs on. We own the internal platforms every employee uses and our collaboration tooling, and we embed engineers directly with Legal, Security, Communications, Product Operations and other business functions to rebuild how their work gets done with Claude at the center. Our mandate is to make Anthropic the best-run company in the world at using its own models internally, and to be the example our customers point to.

We are hiring an engineering leader to run this org. You will lead a growing engineering organization across two tracks: Platforms
, which builds and operates the shared systems the company depends on, and Forward Deployed
, which drops into a business function, proves Claude wins on a real workflow, hands off, and moves on. You will partner on defining the roadmap, build relationships with functional leaders, grow the team, and shape what forward deployed engineering looks like inside a frontier AI lab.

You'll report to the Head of Business Technology and IT, within the Security organization, and you’ll make up the full Business Technology function along with a team of Business Systems Analysts and Product Managers. Together, BizTech partners closely with IT Engineering on corporate systems and endpoints; with Security Engineering on data handling and permissions for agentic workflows; with Labs and Product on dogfooding and the internal builds that become external patterns; with GTM, who point Enterprise customers at this team as the reference for how Anthropic runs internally; and with the leaders of Legal, Workplace, Communications, Product Operations and Product Support, who are your customers.

Responsibilities

Lead and scale a global org of engineers; hire, level and develop the leads under you.
Partner, develop, and execute a year-plus roadmap for how Anthropic's business functions work with Claude, and the success metrics that go with it.
Run the Platforms track: reliability, velocity and scale of Claude Support and the platform layer that every employee depends on.
Run the Forward Deployed track: engagement portfolio, prioritization across functions, handoffs to durable owners, and adoption that actually moves.
Be the technical executive partner to the leaders of Legal, Workplace, Comms, Product Ops and Product Support; make the case for ambitious deployment and for the boundaries on it in the same conversation.
Partner with Labs and Product on dogfooding: feed load-bearing signal back ("here is the eval that shows the gap") and ship internal builds that become external product patterns.
Represent how Anthropic runs internally to Enterprise customers alongside GTM.
Set the engineering bar: production-adjacent builds, eval rigor, reusable patterns, responsible internal deployment with real data and real permissions.

You may be a good fit if you

Have 12+ years in software engineering and 6+ years leading engineers, including at least 3 years managing managers and at least one org of 20+ across multiple domains that you structured yourself
Have run internal-tools, business-systems or platform engineering at a company that added functions faster than it added engineers, and can speak to reliability outcomes on the platform side and adoption outcomes on the embedded side
Lead through technical judgment: whether or not you've been hands-on lately, you can go from an agent architecture to its eval design to its failure modes with your engineers, and your reviews make their builds better
Can walk a General Counsel, a Head of Workplace or a room of senior engineers with strong opinions through a trade-off, make a recommendation, and bring them to a decision they'll commit to
Can hold a high bar on craft while saying no to low-leverage work, and explain the no to the person who asked.
Want real ownership of how a frontier AI lab runs itself on its own models, and care about doing that responsibly — real data, real permissions, real people on the other end

Strong candidates may also have

Forward deployed, software engineering or applied AI leadership experience with external customers.
Product management experience or a track record partnering closely with PMs and analysts.
Experience with corporate systems (Salesforce, Workday, Google Workspace, Slack) at platform scale.
Have built the career rubric or leveling framework for a new kind of engineering role, or stood up a forward deployed function from zero

For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship:
We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification.
Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us.
To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How We're Different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. MACOM (NASDAQ: MTSI) is a global leader in the design and manufacture of advanced semiconductor products across a diverse range of end markets, including Data Centers, Telecommunications, Industrial and Aerospace and Defense. We develop innovative, cutting-edge technologies and products across the spectrum of radio frequency (RF), microwave, millimeter wave, photonics and high-speed analog technologies. Our solutions support critical network infrastructure applications like artificial intelligence, high performance computing, satellite communications, radar, unmanned aerial vehicles, medical equipment, test and measurement and advanced wireless networks.

MACOM has more than 75 years of expertise in semiconductor process development, wafer fabrication, circuit design, advanced packaging, systems architecture and applications engineering. We are committed to our customers’ success. We partner with customers to help solve their most challenging problems by providing semiconductor solutions that are at the forefront of the highest power, highest frequency and/or highest data rates.

Leading technologies, innovative products and driven employees. Come be a part of MACOM and help advance the next generation of connectivity infrastructure!

Director, MMIC Design Engineering

Position Summary

The Director of MMIC Design Engineering provides strategic and technical leadership for MACOM's RF and microwave GaN MMIC product development activities. This role is responsible for leading multiple MMIC development teams, managing a portfolio of GaN-based programs, and driving execution from concept through production release.

The Director serves as a key member of the engineering leadership team, partnering closely with Product Management, Operations, Product Engineering, and Executive Leadership to align technology investments with business objectives and customer requirements. This individual will build organizational capability, accelerate innovation, and drive profitable growth across MACOM's RF and microwave semiconductor portfolio.

Key Responsibilities

Strategic Leadership

Contribute to and execute the short and long-term GaN MMIC product development and technology roadmap.
Align engineering resources and development initiatives with corporate growth objectives and market opportunities.
Evaluate emerging technologies, competitive offerings, and industry trends to identify innovation opportunities.

Engineering Leadership

Lead and develop multiple MMIC design teams responsible for GaN-on-SiC based products.
Establish engineering objectives, organizational structures, and resource plans to achieve development goals.
Build a high-performance culture focused on innovation, accountability, quality, and execution.
Recruit, retain, mentor, and develop world-class engineering talent.
Manage managers, technical leads, and senior individual contributors.

Product Development Execution

Direct multiple concurrent development programs from concept through product qualification and release to production.
Ensure projects meet performance, schedule, cost, quality, yield, and reliability objectives.
Drive development process improvements and best practices across all engineering activities.
Oversee design reviews and provide executive-level technical guidance for critical design decisions.
Ensure effective utilization of Agile development methodologies and project management tools.

Cross-Functional Leadership

Partner with Product Engineering, Operations, Quality, Marketing, and Supply Chain teams to ensure successful product commercialization.
Drive Design for Manufacturability (DFM), Design for Testability (DFT), yield improvement, and product reliability initiatives.
Lead executive program reviews and communicate project status, risks, mitigation plans, and resource requirements.
Facilitate organizational alignment to accelerate time-to-market and maximize business impact.

Customer and Business Engagement

Serve as the senior technical interface for key customers and strategic business opportunities.
Support Product Management in customer visits, technical proposals, feasibility studies, and design-win activities.
Provide executive-level technical leadership during customer escalations and strategic engagements.
Collaborate with business leaders to identify new market opportunities and growth initiatives.

Technology Leadership

Guide architecture and design strategy for advanced RF and microwave GaN MMIC solutions.
Champion innovation in GaN and related semiconductor technologies.
Foster intellectual property development through patents, publications, and proprietary technology advancements.
Establish partnerships with universities, research organizations, foundries, and technology suppliers.

Qualifications

Required

BSEE required; MSEE or PhD preferred.
15+ years of RF, microwave, and MMIC design experience with significant expertise in amplifier design.
5+ years leading engineering organizations, including management of managers and senior technical leaders.
Demonstrated success delivering complex semiconductor products from concept through production.
Extensive knowledge of GaN semiconductor technologies.
Deep understanding of RF and microwave circuit design methodologies.
Strong experience with ADS and RF simulation environments.
Thorough understanding of RF characterization, measurement techniques, product qualification, and reliability testing.
Proven ability to manage multiple development programs simultaneously.
Strong financial acumen, including budget planning and resource management.
Excellent communication, presentation, and executive leadership skills.

Preferred

Experience leading geographically dispersed engineering teams.
Experience supporting defense, aerospace, wireless infrastructure markets.
Proven track record of technology innovation and patent development.
Experience with Agile product development methodologies.
Knowledge of semiconductor manufacturing, packaging, and production operations.

About Salesforce

Salesforce is the #1 AI CRM, where humans with agents drive customer success together. Here, ambition meets action. Tech meets trust. And innovation isn’t a buzzword — it’s a way of life. The world of work as we know it is changing and we're looking for Trailblazers who are passionate about bettering business and the world through AI, driving innovation, and keeping Salesforce's core values at the heart of it all.

Ready to level-up your career at the company leading workforce transformation in the agentic era? You’re in the right place! Agentforce is the future of AI, and you are the future of Salesforce.

The Role

At Salesforce, the Developer Experience & Observability organization is on a mission to deliver a world-class development environment for more than 15,000+ internal engineers. We build the integrated products, platforms, and tooling that engineers – and an increasing number of AI agents – use to take code from idea to production. Our scope spans the full software development lifecycle (SDLC), from local and cloud-based development environments through source control, build systems, testing, code review, CI/CD, deployment and observability.

We are fundamentally reimagining the SDLC for the agentic era. Our ambition goes beyond faster code generation: we are redesigning how engineers and AI agents build software together by removing toil, shortening feedback loops, and helping teams ship high-quality software with confidence. This means turning emerging AI capabilities into trusted developer experiences that work at enterprise scale.

We are looking for a Director of Product Management to join our DX Product Management team. In this role, you will own the strategy, roadmap, and measurable outcomes for key developer products and platforms that sit in the path to production for all Salesforce engineers.

This is a high-impact individual contributor role with broad organizational influence. You will partner closely with engineering and executive leadership, champion developers as customers, and turn their most important problems into products they adopt and value. If you are a product leader who can lay out a clear strategy, dive into technical details, build and experiment with AI tools, and obsess over developer experience, this is your opportunity to be at the forefront of driving impact across thousands of engineers.

In This Position, You Will

Set the product vision and strategy: Define a compelling direction, sequenced roadmap, and investment priorities Translate strategy into clear requirements and iterative delivery. Make deliberate choices about what to build, buy, improve, or retire, balancing developer needs, technical debt, security, cost, and long-term business goals.
Champion the voice of the developer: Build trusted customer relationships through interviews, advisory boards, surveys, workflow research, and product telemetry. Uncover the root causes of developer friction, translate those insights into focused product opportunities, validate solutions, and close the feedback loop.
Drive AI-native developer productivity: Identify opportunities for AI coding tools and agents across the SDLC. Prototype and evaluate emerging tools and workflows, considering quality, developer trust, security, human oversight, and cost. Turn the highest-value experiments into reliable products used in everyday development.
Measure and improve outcomes: Establish baselines and success measures for developer experience, delivery performance, adoption, and AI effectiveness. Combine DORA delivery metrics and SPACE-informed measures with build/test feedback times, CI reliability, developer sentiment and satisfaction measures such as NPS/CSAT, and qualitative research. Use this evidence to identify bottlenecks, prioritize investments, and validate improvements in speed, quality, and satisfaction.
Influence & collaborate at scale: Build strong, trusted partnerships across partner teams and drive influence at all levels of the organization. Resolve competing priorities, navigate technical tradeoffs, and communicate clear recommendations to engineers and executives.
Prioritize high-impact investments: Prioritize the product backlog while balancing developer feedback, technical debt, security requirements, and long-term business goals to maximize platform value.

What We’re Looking For

Product leadership and judgement: 6-10+ years of technical product management experience (or equivalent) with demonstrated success owning large-scale developer platforms, infrastructure platforms, developer tools or DevOps products.
Technical architecture & SDLC fluency: Strong understanding of modern software development practices and developer workflows across source control, build systems, testing, and CI/CD. Experience with complex development environments such as large monolithic applications, monorepos, and/or distributed cloud-native microservices.
AI-native, hands-on approach: You use AI to improve how you work. You can build prototypes, automations, and agents using tools such as Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, or equivalents. Examples include Slack workflows that capture developer feedback, surface recurring issues, and track follow-through.
Customer obsession and analytical rigor: A track record of combining customer research, product data, and experimentation to understand technical users, make better product decisions, and deliver experiences developers adopt and value.
Exceptional communication and influence: The ability to turn complex product and technical tradeoffs into clear written narratives, roadmaps, and executive recommendations while building trust with engineering teams.
Enterprise and trust mindset: Experience building products where scale, security, privacy, compliance, reliability, and performance are fundamental requirements, with an understanding of the additional evaluation and governance considerations for AI tools.
Thriving in ambiguity: Natural comfort with ambiguity and the ability to bring clarity, focus, and alignment across large, matrixed organizations and in a fast-evolving landscape.
Education: BS or MS in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related discipline (or equivalent practical experience).

Preferred Qualifications

Previous experience as a software engineer, engineering leader, or in another technical role.
Prior ownership of an internal developer platform (IDP), service catalog, developer portal, or similar large-scale developer-facing system.
Experience evaluating or deploying AI-assisted software development tools and cloud-based coding agents at scale.
Strong background in developer advocacy or developer relations.

Unleash Your Potential

When you join Salesforce, you’ll be limitless in all areas of your life. Our benefits and resources support you to find balance and be your best , and our AI agents accelerate your impact so you can do your best . Together, we’ll bring the power of Agentforce to organizations of all sizes and deliver amazing experiences that customers love. Apply today to not only shape the future — but to redefine what’s possible — for yourself, for AI, and the world.
